title: URL Shortener Service Requirements Specification
problem_statement: Provide a robust, secure, and persistent HTTP URL shortener service that allows users to create shortened links (with auto-generated codes or custom aliases and optional expiry), redirects callers to the original target while tracking click metrics, provides health checks, and protects against SSRF and abuse.

requirements.text: The service must provide an endpoint to shorten a target URL using an auto-generated unique code.
acceptance_criteria: POST /shorten with body {"url": "https://example.com/very/long/path"} returns HTTP 201 with body containing a generated string 'code' and full 'short_url'.
Subsequent requests with different URLs receive distinct, non-colliding generated codes.

requirements.text: The service must allow clients to specify a custom unique alias during link creation and reject duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: POST /shorten with body {"url": "https://example.com", "custom_alias": "my-link"} returns HTTP 201 with code 'my-link'.
POST /shorten with body {"url": "https://other.com", "custom_alias": "my-link"} when 'my-link' already exists returns HTTP 409 Conflict with an error message indicating the alias is already in use.

requirements.text: The service must redirect requests for valid short codes to the original target URL and increment the link's click count.
acceptance_criteria: GET /{code} for an active code redirects to the original target URL with HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect and Location header matching the target URL.
GET /{code} for a non-existent code returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
Each successful GET /{code} increases total click count by 1 and updates last_visited_at to the current timestamp.

requirements.text: The service must support optional expiration for links and reject redirection once expired.
acceptance_criteria: POST /shorten with {"url": "https://example.com", "expires_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"} stores the expiration timestamp.
GET /{code} executed after the specified expiration timestamp returns HTTP 404 Not Found and does not increment click count.

requirements.text: The service must provide an analytics endpoint returning total clicks, creation timestamp, and last visited timestamp for a code.
acceptance_criteria: GET /analytics/{code} for a newly created link with 0 visits returns HTTP 200 with {"total_clicks": 0, "created_at": "<ISO-8601>", "last_visited_at": null}.
GET /analytics/{code} following a visit returns HTTP 200 with updated 'total_clicks' count and an ISO-8601 'last_visited_at' timestamp.
GET /analytics/{code} for a non-existent code returns HTTP 404 Not Found.

requirements.text: The service must expose a health check endpoint for load balancers indicating operational status.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health when database and service are operational returns HTTP 200 OK with body {"status": "healthy"}.
GET /health when backing datastore is unavailable returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable.

requirements.text: The service must prevent SSRF and unsafe protocols by strictly validating target URLs before shortening.
acceptance_criteria: POST /shorten with URL using non-HTTP(S) scheme (e.g., 'ftp://example.com', 'javascript:alert(1)') returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.

POST /shorten with target resolving to loopback or private IP ranges (e.g., 'http://localhost', 'http://127.0.0.1:8080', 'http://169.254.169.254', 'http://10.0.0.1', 'http://[::1]') returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with an SSRF prevention error.
POST /shorten with a public domain that resolves to a private IP address returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.

requirements.text: The service must enforce per-client rate limiting on link creation to mitigate spam and denial of service.
acceptance_criteria: Exceeding the configured threshold of POST /shorten calls from a single client IP within a rate-limit window returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header.
Requests within the allowed rate limit window succeed with HTTP 201.

requirements.text: The service must persist all shortened URLs, metadata, and analytics data across application restarts.
acceptance_criteria: Create link 'abc' via POST /shorten, stop the service process, restart the service, and verify GET /abc returns HTTP 307 and GET /analytics/abc returns previous click history.

requirements.text: The service codebase must provide comprehensive automated tests and clear documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Running the test suite executes automated tests covering all endpoints (POST /shorten, GET /{code}, GET /analytics/{code}, GET /health) including success, validation errors, expired links, and rate limits.
A README.md exists in repository root detailing environment setup, execution commands, testing commands, and endpoint API contract documentation.

assumptions: HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect is used instead of HTTP 301 Permanent Redirect so that user-agents do not cache the redirection locally, ensuring every click hits the server for analytics tracking.
Client identity for rate-limiting is determined by client remote IP or a validated 'X-Forwarded-For' header when behind a trusted reverse proxy.
Generated short codes use Base62 alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) with a default minimum length of 7 characters.
Custom aliases are constrained to alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores with length between 3 and 64 characters.
Database storage uses an embedded or network SQL/key-value store persisting to disk to fulfill restart survivability.

open_questions.question: Should GET /{code} return HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect or HTTP 301 Permanent Redirect?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HTTP 301 is aggressively cached by browsers, preventing repeat visits by the same client from hitting the server and undercounting analytics.
open_questions.proposed_default: Use HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect to ensure all visits are tracked in analytics.

open_questions.question: What schema and format should be used for link expiration in the POST /shorten request payload?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines request payload validation, serialization, and whether clients supply an absolute timestamp (e.g., ISO 8601) or a relative TTL in seconds.
open_questions.proposed_default: Accept an optional ISO-8601 UTC timestamp string in field 'expires_at'.

open_questions.question: What is the exact rate limit policy (capacity and window) for POST /shorten per client IP?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Directly affects client experience, load testing thresholds, and security bounds.
open_questions.proposed_default: Limit to 60 requests per minute per IP address.

open_questions.question: Should expired links retain their analytics or be purged, and can an expired custom alias be reclaimed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Affects data retention policies, GET /analytics behavior on expired codes, and unique constraint indexing.
open_questions.proposed_default: Retain expired link records for analytics access (GET /analytics/{code} still accessible with an 'expired': true flag), and prevent alias reuse to avoid link hijacking.

out_of_scope: User registration, authentication, API keys, or role-based access control.
Editing target URLs or manual deletion of created short links.
Advanced analytics dimensions such as referrer tracking, geolocation, user-agent parsing, or timeseries click graphs.
Custom branded domains or DNS configuration management.
